solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 5 across to 4); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take in selected news items?

definitions.meaning: to take in food or information is to absorb and process it
a summary compilation of chosen news stories

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether absorbing a curated selection of news headlines counts as keeping informed.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbing food or facts is the verb sense; a compiled summary of stories is the noun sense of the same word.

clue.text: Smart to sample book, including pages lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the letters run upwards, read in reverse
including means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: to read is to sample a book

explanation.surface: A smart person dips into a book, including turning some pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' is the definition, not part of the sampling; 'lifted' reverses everything because in a down light the letters then run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatly and stylishly dressed is a description of a smart appearance.

clue.text: See fellow ignoring new topics — wise

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letter named

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman or fellow
themes are topics
sage means wise

explanation.surface: A man disregards the latest subjects of discussion and is deemed wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'I see' means one understands, which is the idiom of grasping what is meant.

clue.text: Society of current importance, stripped of power, but not complaining

indicators.note: stripped of means having the letter named removed

parts.note: topical means relevant to current affairs
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A newsworthy society loses its influence but bears it without grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Enduring hardship without grumbling is the philosophical calm associated with the ancient Stoics.

clue.text: Favouring appropriate trading success

parts.note: to be pro something is to be in favour of it
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A business commentator praises some suitably successful commercial dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Money gained from buying and selling is the measure of commercial success, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fast driver, expert in Rolls Royce initially

indicators.note: in puts the expert inside the two initials
initially means taking the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A speedy motorist proves skilled at the wheel of a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in motor sport drives at speed, so the word names a fast driver.

clue.text: Melange of April's seafood? It's in your dreams

indicators.note: a melange is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mixed seafood platter served on the first of April might be a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: The April reference hints at April Fools' Day pranks, fitting the dupe in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of happiness based on illusion exists only in imagination, which is what living in a dream suggests.

clue.text: Complication no good in story

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A plot twist that adds nothing to a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddled knot or confused situation is a complication or mess.

clue.text: Score at snooker with difficulty — uneven surface?

parts.note: potting a ball is how points are scored in snooker
being in a hole means being in difficulty

explanation.surface: A snooker player struggles to score on a table whose cloth is bumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a British cue game in which points come from sinking balls into pockets. The question mark flags the definition as an example: a road hollow is one kind of uneven surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity in a road makes it bumpy, so the crater is an example of a rough, uneven surface.

clue.text: Index Pete devised as means to an end

indicators.note: devised means invented or worked out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Pete created an index purely for convenience.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun it names a convenient measure taken to achieve something, a means to an end.

clue.text: Limits to comedian embracing depressed funny man

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece within its arms
the limits of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: feeling low means feeling depressed

explanation.surface: A comic hugs a gloomy fellow comedian to cheer him up.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus jester is a comic performer, so he is literally a funny man.

clue.text: System of morals? This runs short in the City

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the City's letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: running short means losing the final letter of the word before

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: A worried observer suspects the financial district lacks any moral code.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral code or principle is a set of values guiding conduct, matching a system of morals.

clue.text: Certain to return, enthralled by friend reading

indicators.note: being enthralled by means being held captive within the other word

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: returning means the word for certain runs backwards

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A friend is captivated by a book and sure to come back for more.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful read of a text, the act of scrutinising it, is what the noun names.

clue.text: Model stumbling — damage after twisting — a scene that's overwrought

indicators.note: stumbling suggests things falling out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: twisting means the word for damage is turned round

parts.note: to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: A fashion model trips on the catwalk, and a twisted ankle leads to a dramatic fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' reads as a noun in the surface, but it works as the verb, and 'after twisting' both turns it round and places it after the jumbled model.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational, exaggerated display of emotion is an overwrought scene, the figurative sense of the stage genre.

clue.text: Historic item? Not in favour and quite dismissing it

parts.note: anti means opposed or not in favour

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away the letters named

parts.note: taken as written before letters are removed

explanation.surface: An old object is out of fashion and somewhat rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: An old collectable valued for its age is an example of a historic item, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Poorly written blog almost all of international relevance

indicators.note: something poorly written is badly put together, so the letters are jumbled
almost means the last letter is dropped from the word for all

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: A sloppily written blog post is nearly all about world affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldwide in scope, it describes something relevant across all nations.

clue.text: Very favoured by clan not wanting the Italian notoriety

parts.note: to be in is to be fashionable or much favoured

indicators.note: not wanting means leaving out the letters named

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
il is an Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A well-liked clan rejects its Italian connections and becomes notorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being famous for something bad is disgrace or ill repute, which is notoriety.

clue.text: Liberal is a little flexible

parts.note: some means a little or a certain amount

explanation.surface: A politician of the Liberal party shows a little give on policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and graceful in body, the word describes someone lithe and bendy.

clue.text: Old piano — time for some work by Mozart?

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An old piano is the focus of time spent on a Mozart piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magic Flute is a staged musical drama by Mozart; such stage works are an example of his output.

clue.text: An American writer or two

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a pair or two

explanation.surface: Someone tries to name one or two US authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain is the pen name of Samuel Clemens; the same word is an old poetic form of the number following one.

clue.text: Support a couple

definitions.meaning: a strut or prop that holds something steady
a pair, especially of game birds

explanation.surface: A request for help from two people.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop that holds something rigid is one sense; a pair of shot pheasants is the other.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink quite abused by the French

indicators.note: abused means misused or mistreated, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: French people are said to have quite mistreated a particular spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican spirit distilled from agave is one specific alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Set about reversing small scope for manoeuvre

indicators.note: about means going around the other piece

parts.note: to lay something is to set it down

indicators.note: reversing means the word for small is read backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone sets about backing a small vehicle into a space with little room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set about' looks like a phrase meaning begin, but 'about' is the containment signal and 'reversing' turns the Scottish word for small round.
explanation.definitionFit: Room to deviate or freedom of action is the latitude a person has, originally the sideways drift of a ship.

clue.text: This writer is enthralled by revolutionary year? Correct

indicators.note: being enthralled by means being held inside the other word

parts.note: red is a common term for a revolutionary or communist
the setter referring to themself, giving me

explanation.surface: An author captivated by a revolutionary year asks whether that's right.
explanation.definitionFit: To put right a fault or ill is to fix it, the verb sense of a cure.
